display.purpose: Page titles. The largest type in the product; there is no hero scale.

title.purpose: Card titles, heavier and tighter than the headings above them.

body.purpose: Running copy, table cells, field values.

label.purpose: Buttons and form labels. Same size as body, distinguished by weight alone.

data.purpose: Machine-shaped content only: ids, shas, paths, code, aligned figures.

review.purpose: The pull request review surface body and identity size (13px). Between dense metadata and ordinary body.

micro.purpose: Small labels and chips inside the review surface (11px).

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: A surface that has left the page plane. Opens with a 1px inset top highlight so it reads as lit from above.

shadows.name: elevated
shadows.purpose: A surface floating over unrelated content and dismissible: dialog, popover, dropdown.

shadows.name: card-resting
shadows.purpose: The near-imperceptible shadow-sm carried by every ordinary card. Softens the edge; does not lift.

motion.name: fade-up
motion.purpose: Signature entrance for content arriving after load: 8px rise with fade.

motion.name: collapse
motion.purpose: Accordion and collapsible open/close against the Radix content-height variable.

motion.name: skeleton-wave
motion.purpose: Loading placeholder: sweeps a Panel L3 to L4 gradient across the block.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single amber action on a screen. Dark type on a lit field.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 12px; min-height: 40px; padding: 10px 20px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; font-family: "DM Sans", sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--color-primary-light, #f8b76d); color: var(--color-primary-dark, #443024); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.2); } .ds-btn-primary:active { filter: brightness(1.2); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--color-card-lv3, #30304b); }

components.name: Primary Dark Button
components.description: Amber text on the amber's own deep twin. Emphasis without spending the accent.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary-dark { background: var(--color-primary-dark, #443024); color: var(--color-primary-light, #f8b76d); } .ds-btn-primary-dark:hover { filter: brightness(1.2); } .ds-btn-primary-dark:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--color-card-lv3, #30304b); }

components.name: Helper Button
components.description: Neutral action inside a card. Panel L2 ground, secondary text.
components.css: .ds-btn-helper { background: var(--color-card-lv2, #202032); color: var(--color-text-secondary, #cdcddf); } .ds-btn-helper:hover { filter: brightness(1.2); } .ds-btn-helper:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--color-card-lv3, #30304b); }

components.name: Cancel Button
components.description: No ground at all. Tertiary text that rises to primary on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-cancel { background: transparent; color: var(--color-text-tertiary, rgba(243,243,247,0.5)); } .ds-btn-cancel:hover { color: var(--color-text-primary, #ffffff); } .ds-btn-cancel:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--color-card-lv3, #30304b); }

components.name: Status Button
components.description: Status hue as text on a very dark tinted ground of the same hue. Never a filled status colour.
components.css: .ds-btn-status-error { background: #271720; color: var(--color-danger, #fa5867); min-height: 32px; padding: 8px 16px; } .ds-btn-status-error:hover { filter: brightness(1.2); } .ds-btn-status-error:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--color-card-lv3, #30304b); }

components.name: Badge
components.description: A decorative xs button in a pill. Not a separate component: pass a different button variant to restyle it.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; min-height: 28px; padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-primary-dark, #443024); color: var(--color-primary-light, #f8b76d); font-family: "DM Sans", sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The resting surface. Borderless; depth comes from the tonal step, not from a shadow.
components.html:
Advanced settings

Reasoning, sampling, and rate limits for this model.

Empty uses the model default.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 12px; background: var(--color-card-lv1, #181825); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.05); font-family: "DM Sans", sans-serif; } .ds-card-header { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; padding: 24px; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; color: var(--color-text-primary, #ffffff); } .ds-card-desc { margin: 0; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--color-text-secondary, #cdcddf); } .ds-card-content { padding: 0 24px 24px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--color-text-secondary, #cdcddf); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Panel L2 ground outlined by a ring, not a border. Focus thickens the ring and brightens the field.
components.css: .ds-input { display: flex; width: 100%; align-items: center; height: 40px; padding: 0 20px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; background: var(--color-card-lv2, #202032); color: var(--color-text-primary, #ffffff); font-family: "DM Sans", sans-serif; font-size: 14px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--color-card-lv3, #30304b); transition: box-shadow 0.15s, filter 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--color-text-tertiary, rgba(243,243,247,0.5)); } .ds-input:hover { filter: brightness(1.2); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--color-card-lv3, #30304b); filter: brightness(1.2); } .ds-input[data-invalid] { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--color-danger, #fa5867); } .ds-input[data-invalid]:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--color-danger, #fa5867); }

components.name: Skeleton
components.description: Loading placeholder. A wave sweeps a Panel L3 to L4 gradient across the block.
components.css: .ds-skeleton { height: 16px; width: 220px; border-radius: 6px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--color-card-lv3, #30304b) 0%, #3d3d5c 50%, var(--color-card-lv3, #30304b) 100%); background-size: 200% 100%; animation: ds-skeleton-wave 1.8s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-skeleton-wave { 0% { background-position: -200% 0; } 100% { background-position: 200% 0; } }

narrative.overview:
A dark room full of instruments. Everything is legible under low light, nothing competes for attention on its own, and a single amber lamp lights only what needs a decision. The product's own vocabulary already says this out loud — the leader's landing surface is called the Cockpit — and the visual system is built for the person watching a practice run rather than the person being reviewed.

The system is dense and efficient before it is comfortable. This is a working instrument for someone who arrives with a question, so information per pixel outranks breathing room, and spacing tightens rather than paginates when a surface carries real data. Density is never bought with noise: surfaces are borderless, flat, and quiet, and hierarchy comes from how light a panel is, not from lines drawn between things.

The most distinctive decision in the system is how it responds to touch. Hover and active states do not change colour — they raise brightness. A button lit by the amber lamp gets brighter under the cursor; it never becomes a different button. The palette stays fixed while the light moves across it, which is what keeps a dense screen calm.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black blue-violet ground (#101019) with three tonal panel steps above it
Exactly one accent — Signal Amber — carrying every primary action
State expressed as light (brightness, focus ring), never as a colour swap
Borderless surfaces; separation by tone, not by rule
Generous 12px corners on every interactive surface, against tight interior spacing
DM Sans throughout, Overpass Mono reserved for data and code

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Signal Amber is the only accent in the system. A screen has one amber region — the thing to do next. If two elements are amber, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Cool Ground Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is tinted blue-violet, never neutral grey. A pure #1a1a1a panel dropped into this system reads as a foreign element immediately, because it removes the temperature contrast the accent depends on.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Not-Accent Rule
rules.body: Success, danger, warning, alert, and info are semantic and never decorative. They never stand in for the accent, and the accent never stands in for them.

rules.name: The Small-h3 Rule
rules.body: The third heading level is deliberately 0.875rem — the same size as body — and reads as a label, not a heading. Do not fix it upward to fit a conventional scale; a section this deep should announce itself by weight and position, not by size.

rules.name: The Weight-Over-Size Rule
rules.body: Below the headline level, hierarchy is carried by weight (400 to 600 to 700) at a fixed 0.875rem. Reach for weight before reaching for a new size.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-For-Data Rule
rules.body: Overpass Mono marks content that is machine-shaped: shas, model ids, paths, code, aligned figures. It is never used for personality, section labels, or emphasis.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: To make something feel higher, move it up a panel step. Reach for a shadow only when the surface genuinely floats over unrelated content and can be dismissed.

rules.name: The Inset Highlight Rule
rules.body: Both shadows open with a 1px inset white highlight along the top edge. That highlight is what makes a floating surface read as lit from above in a dark room; a hand-written shadow that omits it will look flat and out of place.

rules.name: The No-Literal-Size Rule
rules.body: Every size in the system has a name. If a surface needs a step that does not exist, add it to @theme and document it — do not write text-[13px] in a component. A literal is invisible to the design system, so nothing keeps the next one consistent with it, and half-pixel values are the reliable symptom that this rule was skipped.

rules.name: The Visible-Focus Rule
rules.body: A focus ring is drawn with the dedicated --color-ring token (#f59220), never with the structural card-lv3. card-lv3 on a resting card measures 1.38:1, under the 3:1 WCAG 2.1 requires of a focus indicator; --color-ring measures 5.46:1 to 8.12:1 on every surface. A thick ring in a colour nobody can see is worse than a thin one, because it looks solved.

dos: Do express interaction as light. Hover and active are brightness-120; focus is ring-3. A new component that changes colour on hover is inconsistent with everything around it.
Do reach for a tonal step before a shadow when something needs to feel higher.
Do define a new button variant as a --button-background / --button-foreground pair, and let the base class do the rest.
Do use the deep twin of a hue (amber-deep, lavender-deep, blush-deep) when you need emphasis without spending the accent.
Do keep Overpass Mono for machine-shaped content — ids, shas, paths, code, aligned figures.
Do use 12px corners on interactive surfaces, and reserve the 4 / 6 / 8px scale for small interior details.
Do tighten spacing before paginating when a surface carries a lot of data. Density is the intent.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent. Signal Amber is the only one, and a screen has one amber region.
Don't use a status colour decoratively, or the accent to mean success or danger.
Don't put a border on a card. Separation is tonal; where an outline is required, use a ring.
Don't use a neutral grey. Every neutral in this system is tinted blue-violet, and an untinted panel reads as foreign.
Don't enlarge h3 to fit a conventional type scale — it is label-sized on purpose.
Don't build a separate badge component; a badge is a decorative xs button.
Don't let the interface drift toward a consumer product: no illustration, no emoji as section markers, no pastel palette spread across a surface, no animated tone. The user is working.
Don't imitate an IDE or code editor: syntax highlighting is content, not identity, and editor chrome, panel density, and tab metaphors belong to the tool Kodus sits beside, not inside.
Don't write a literal font size in a component. Use a named step, or add one to @theme and document it. A half-pixel value is always a mistake.
